slides.title: Short-Circuit Logic
slides.prompt: In logical operations, evaluation stops as soon as the outcome is guaranteed.
slides.codeSnippet:
bool a = false && (5 / 0 == 1); // Second part skipped (safe)
bool b = true || (5 / 0 == 1);  // Second part skipped (safe)

slides.title: Short-Circuit AND Condition

slides.title: Short-Circuit OR Behavior
slides.prompt: In 'true || expr', why is 'expr' never executed?
options: Because the result is already guaranteed to be true
Because OR operator has lowest priority
slides.correctAnswer: Because the result is already guaranteed to be true

slides.title: Benefit of Short-Circuit
slides.prompt: What primary programming advantage does short-circuiting offer?
options: Allows safe conditional checks without risking crashes or illegal operations

slides.title: Bitwise vs Logical Evaluation
slides.prompt: Do bitwise operators (& and |) support short-circuit evaluation?
options: No, bitwise operators always evaluate both operands
slides.correctAnswer: No, bitwise operators always evaluate both operands
